subject: Expo visitor flow & swag distribution scenarios
messages:
From: Claire Huang <claire@cortexcloud.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Redwood booth — queueing & swag plans

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for confirming the corner booth at Interop. I wanted to flag two things we need from your team to finalize the floorplan:

- Expected peak flow per 15 minutes (rough estimate).
- Whether you want an open-flow demo area or a gated queueed line for demos.
- Any powered-swag dispenser requirements (we have a limited handful of power drops on that aisle).

Also: the show ops team asked for a contingency for 400+ simultaneous attendees — can you confirm if you plan to run lead capture tablets inside the line or at the demo table?

If you can send a scribble or drawing that shows the preferred queue routing, we can lock the peninsula space and produce a permit-friendly layout.

Appreciate it — Claire
Claire Huang
Events Lead, CortexCloud
claire@cortexcloud.com
Office: +1 415-555-0189

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
To: Claire Huang <claire@cortexcloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-29T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood booth — queueing & swag plans

Claire — thanks for the heads up. Quick answers up front:

- Peak flow estimate: 120–160 visitors per 15 minutes during the key 45-minute block after keynote.
- We prefer a short gated queue for scheduled demos (2 demo stations) plus an open engagement area for quick product look-ins. Goal is to keep demo wait under 8 minutes.
- Swag dispenser: we want a powered, staff-attended dispenser (photo below). If power is constrained, we can fallback to staff-handout from a locked chest.

Attached: redwood_expo_floorplan_v3.pdf (2-up plan) and swag-station-schematic_v2.png. Key notes in the PDF:
  • Queue ingress at the north-side aisle (keeps flow away from main thoroughfare)
  • Two demo pedestals centered on back wall, each with 2x lead-capture tablets
  • Staff handoff station to the left with one power drop preferred

Ask: can you confirm whether the peninsula allows 48" queue barriers (vendor-supplied) or if we need to use freestanding stanchions? That affects sightlines and permit language.

Thanks — looping Marissa for signage and Sean for logistics readiness.

—
Naomi Feldman
Field Marketing Manager | Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com
cell: +1 312-555-0193

> Attached: redwood_expo_floorplan_v3.pdf (2-up plan) and swag-station-schematic_v2.png.

Thanks Naomi — the layout looks good overall. A few operational points from signage/print:

- For the gated queue we need a 24" high branded mesh banner on the front of the barrier (we'll provide artwork).
- Wayfinding: please confirm copy for the overhead placard — we have two options: "Live Demos" or "Product Surge + Live Demos". Recommend short copy.
- Collateral: we'll order 1,000 one-pagers and 500 product cards; can we store 200 of the one-pagers in the demo crates for overnight restock?

Operational ask for Claire/Expo Ops: if the peninsula requires anchored barrier, we need the permit addendum by EOD Thursday so our fabricator can change hardware.

Attachment: (none) — I'll drop print specs in the shared drive and tag Naomi.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Events Producer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Hi team — quick update from Expo Ops and AV:

- Peninsulas in Hall B allow up to 48" anchored barriers but only with a signed liability waiver. I attached the waiver PDF to the shared drive.
- Power: we can guarantee a single 20A drop at the staff handoff station. If you need additional power for a dispenser, bring an approved battery backup or confirm you will use manual handout.
- Permit addendum: we can turn that around by Thursday 18:00 PT if you submit the hardware change request today.

Marissa — we'll expect the banner copy and print specs by EOD. Naomi — we'll book a 30-min slot on Thursday for a virtual walk-through with the show floor manager.

Thanks — Claire
Claire Huang
